report:
## Conclusion: The claim is TRUE

Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, 19.5 mg) is FDA-approved for prevention of pregnancy for up to five years. This is well-supported by multiple authoritative sources:

**Regulatory approval:** The FDA approved Kyleena in 2016 specifically for "prevention of pregnancy for up to five years," as confirmed by the official Bayer press release announcing the approval (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-bayers-kyleena-levonorgestrel-releasing-intrauterine-system-195-mg-for-prevention-of-pregnancy-for-up-to-five-years-300330006.html) and the FDA-approved drug label itself, which states "Kyleena should not remain in the uterus after 5 years" (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080).

**Clinical trial evidence:** The FDA's own summary review of the Kyleena New Drug Application reports the pivotal Phase III trial data underlying this approval: the cumulative five-year pregnancy rate, calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method, was 1.4 per 100 women (95% CI 0.8–2.5), demonstrating sustained contraceptive efficacy across the full five-year period (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208224Orig1s000SumR.pdf).

**Independent confirmation:** Manufacturer and consumer health resources consistently corroborate the five-year duration, noting that Kyleena is intended to be replaced after five years if continued contraception is desired (https://www.kyleena-us.com/kyleena-effectiveness/how-does-kyleena-work).

**Bottom line:** This is a well-documented, FDA-verified fact supported by both regulatory labeling and the pivotal clinical trial data used for approval — not merely a marketing claim.
